cues.text: During digital innovation planning sessions at the International Telecommunication Union, or ITU, regional projects, executives proposed cloud-based collaboration systems supporting distributed global teams.
The question asks: the intended operational improvement would most likely produce which of the following?
Option A: complete independence from external infrastructure and vendor ecosystems.
Option B: reduced customer interaction through centralised communication restrictions.
Option C: elimination of cybersecurity responsibilities across collaborative environments.
Option D: enhanced collaboration through unified communication and remote accessibility.
The suggested answer is D.
Shared cloud tools enable distributed teams to communicate and collaborate.
Notice why the others fail: a cloud system actually increases reliance on external providers, it does not restrict customer interaction, and it never removes cybersecurity responsibilities.
Next, CA Q9.
Within an operational resilience exercise at Zenith Bank Nigeria Plc, cybersecurity analysts identified phishing attacks targeting online banking customers.
Which IT management principle is most directly involved in mitigating this threat?
Option A: value delivery through customer acquisition and product diversification.
Option B: risk management through proactive identification of cybersecurity threats.
Option C: resource coordination through strategic outsourcing of IT operations.
Option D: performance optimisation through centralised monitoring dashboards.
The suggested answer is B.
Proactive threat identification is risk management.
The analysts are spotting a threat before it causes harm, and that is the core of managing risk.
Next, CA Q10.
Concurrently reviewing operational inefficiencies at Airtel Networks Nigeria Limited, technology strategists recommended automation of repetitive customer support processes.
Which organisational benefit of IT management is most directly targeted?
Option A: risk governance through centralised policy documentation and audit controls.
Option B: speed through automation and real-time transaction processing capabilities.
Option C: regulatory compliance through stricter vendor acquisition and screening rules.
Option D: resource decentralisation through independent departmental infrastructure models.
The suggested answer is B.
Automation reduces manual processing time and improves speed.
Repetitive support tasks are exactly where automation saves time.
Next, CA Q11.
During a digital transformation review conducted at Access Bank Nigeria Plc, stakeholders observed that newly deployed platforms failed because employees continued using manual processes.
Which challenge of IT management best explains this outcome?
Option A: cultural resistance resulting from low digital literacy and workflow habits.
Option B: performance measurement failures involving weak service-level agreements.
Option C: regulatory uncertainty involving overlapping financial compliance directives.
Option D: infrastructure instability caused by insufficient cloud migration strategies.
The suggested answer is A.
Continued manual habits indicate cultural resistance.
The technology was deployed, but people kept to their old ways of working, which points to a people and culture problem rather than a technical or regulatory one.
Next, CA Q13.

Following ransomware preparedness exercises conducted at Rack Centre Data Infrastructure Limited, executives instructed IT teams to create formal disaster recovery documentation and incident response procedures.
Which management function is most directly demonstrated?
Option A: planning through development of risk mitigation and recovery strategies.
Option B: directing through continuous employee engagement and communication activities.
Option C: organising through departmental restructuring and reporting alignment controls.
Option D: staffing through workforce expansion and specialised talent acquisition efforts.
The suggested answer is A.
Recovery documentation defines future responses, which is planning.
